title: Toward Reliable Probabilistic CHF Prediction: Physical Interpretation and Evaluation of Epistemic–Aleatoric Uncertainty Decomposition
abstract: Critical heat flux (CHF) is a key thermal-hydraulic phenomenon in reactor safety; however, its accurate prediction remains challenging due to highly nonlinear behavior. Accordingly, data-driven models have been developed to overcome limitations of conventional correlations. Although probabilistic neural networks provide uncertainty estimates alongside predictions, the reliability of their calibration and consistency with the underlying data distribution remain unclear. A unified framework is proposed to evaluate uncertainty reliability using 24,579 CHF data points and three probabilistic approaches: Bayesian neural networks, Monte Carlo Dropout, and Deep Ensembles. Calibration is assessed using AUSE, CE, and NLL, while uncertainty consistency is evaluated through Spearman correlation between epistemic uncertainty and data sparsity measures. The results reveal that epistemic uncertainty across models is more strongly influenced by prediction magnitude than data sparsity, indicating limited consistency with the underlying data distribution. To improve the uncertainty calibration and consistency of the probabilistic framework, a pruned diversified deep ensemble (PDiv-DE) is proposed. The PDiv-DE preserves predictive performance while improving calibration accuracy and strengthening the consistency between epistemic uncertainty and data sparsity. Therefore, the proposed framework provides a practical step toward more reliable uncertainty quantification for CHF prediction and supports the development of data-driven models for safety-relevant thermal-hydraulic applications.

title: Public valuation of a partial transition from large reactors to enhanced-safety small modular reactors: Evidence from South Korea
abstract: This study estimates South Korean households’ willingness to pay (WTP) for a proposed partial transition from conventional large reactors to enhanced-safety small modular reactors (SMRs). The scenario maintains total capacity at 1,400 MW while replacing 700 MW of conventional large-reactor capacity with SMRs. A nationwide contingent valuation survey of 1,000 household heads or spouses, conducted in early 2026, employed one-and-one-half-bound dichotomous-choice questions and a spike model to accommodate zero WTP responses. Mean monthly WTP was KRW 2,677 (USD 1.74) in the model without covariates and KRW 2,591 (USD 1.68) in the covariate model. WTP was positively associated with household income and prior SMR knowledge and negatively associated with the presence of children. The treatment of stated zero responses materially affects the estimated welfare measure, and the high prevalence of payment-vehicle protests underscores the importance of financing design and perceived institutional responsibility. The results indicate that the proposed transition has measurable non-market value; however, the estimate reflects households’ valuation of the bundled policy scenario—including changes in reactor technology, unit scale, capacity composition, and safety-related characteristics—rather than the marginal value of passive safety or any individual SMR attribute.

title: A reliability data aggregation method for fusion-oriented research facilities
abstract: This paper aims to develop a statistical method for integrating multiple incomplete data sources to improve the estimation of the failure-rate probability distribution of fusion-specific devices. The data aggregation approach proposed in this work is to support the Reliability, Availability, Maintainability, and Inspectability (RAMI) studies for fusion-oriented research facilities. This work focuses on developing a procedure for handling missing or incomplete data from multiple sources, as well as formulating a statistical framework for combining data from different sources that refer to the same equipment type and failure mode. Specifically, a Bayesian result is adopted under the assumption of a constant failure rate over time. This framework motivates the use of the Gamma distributions to model the failure-rate parameter of each device. Subsequently, two alternative procedures are introduced to approximate, using a single Gamma distribution, the weighted mixture formed by combining Gamma distributions corresponding to the same equipment type across multiple data sources. The proposed method is validated through an extensive simulation study and further illustrated by application to the accelerator systems of the IFMIF-DONES facility. Finally, the proposed algorithm has been implemented in the open-source software R to facilitate its use in the nuclear fusion community.

title: Numerical study of thermal mixing characteristics in lead-bismuth parallel triple-jet based on detached eddy simulation
abstract: In lead-cooled fast reactors (LFRs), the temperature difference between hot and cold lead–bismuth eutectic (LBE) streams from different fuel assemblies can exceed 100 K. Their interaction in the upper plenum generates complex turbulent jets, which may cause thermal striping and thermal fatigue in structural components, making thermal mixing critical to reactor safety. Conventional RANS methods struggle to reliably capture transient temperature fluctuations, while pure LES incurs prohibitively high computational cost for multi-condition engineering studies. Detached eddy simulation (DES), which combines near-wall Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes modeling with large eddy simulation in separated regions, strikes a practical balance between eddy-resolving capability and computational efficiency, providing an efficient approach for resolving large-scale turbulent structures and temperature fluctuations. In this study, DES was used to investigate the thermal mixing of hot and cold LBE coolant jets in a parallel triple-jet configuration. The method was validated against liquid-sodium triple-jet experimental data and then applied to examine the effects of inlet velocity and temperature difference. The results show that higher inlet velocity enhances jet inertia, delays near-inlet mixing, and broadens the frequency range of temperature fluctuations, whereas a larger temperature difference mainly increases temperature gradients and fluctuation intensity, with little influence on the overall flow structure and dominant frequency range. A reference comparison with LES data further demonstrates that DES can reproduce the overall dependence of temperature fluctuation intensity on the operating parameters with comparable fluctuation amplitude ranges, while requiring approximately 94 % lower estimated computational cost.

title: Proactive maintenance and structural modifications of VVER-1000 steam generator blowdown systems to ensure long-term safety
abstract: Steam generators of VVER-1000 pressurized water reactors play a crucial role in separating the primary and secondary circuits and safely removing heat from the reactor core. This paper systematically evaluates the degradation mechanisms on the secondary side of the steam generator, focusing on the continuous blowdown and sludge removal systems in the context of ensuring long-term safety functions. Based on operational data and experience from a reference nuclear power plant, a transition from reactive to proactive preventive maintenance is proposed. This approach combines continuous diagnostics, water chemistry management, technical modifications to piping layouts, and risk-based planning. The study identifies dominant damage mechanisms (pitting corrosion, stress corrosion cracking, sludge accumulation in inspection pockets, and foreign material ingress), quantifies their impact on the integrity of heat transfer tubes, and proposes practical measures to maintain the barrier function of the steam generator. The benefits include a reduced probability of failures, stabilization of the water chemistry regime, shortened outage durations, and improved long-term reliability of Safety Class 1 components.

title: Numerical study on effects of tube bundle geometry and arrangement on external steam-air condensation
abstract: Condensation of steam mixed with non-condensable gases (NCGs) is a key physical process governing containment depressurization and thermal removal during severe nuclear reactor accidents. Previous studies on steam condensation with NCGs outside tube bundles have mostly focused on bundle structures with a single length and pitch. This paper examines the effects of bundle length, pitch, inclination angle, arrangement, and tube rows number on steam-air condensation outside tube bundles via numerical simulation. The coupling effects between tube length and arrangement, as well as tube pitch and inclination angle, are also analyzed. Calculations indicate that for tubes of different lengths and arrangements, the condensation heat transfer coefficient (CHTC) first decreases and then stabilizes as the tube length increases. Furthermore, the CHTC of different tubes within the bundle increases with larger tube pitch. At a tube pitch of 1.5d, tube innermost tube exhibits the poorest heat transfer performance. At a tube pitch of 3d, its heat transfer capacity becomes 2.55 times that under the 1.5d condition. Inclination induces more obvious overlap effect with narrow tube pitch, at a pitch of 2d, and the overall CHTC of the bundle increases with a larger inclination angle. Additionally, the overall CHTC for a 1m tube bundle gradually increases with increased tube rows, the CHTC surpasses that of a single tube when the number of rows exceeds 10. For 3m and 5m tube bundles, it initially decreases and then tends to stabilize as the number of rows increases.

title: Effects of curvature and inclination on external steam condensation with non-condensable gases under natural convection
abstract: Steam-air condensation is a significant heat transfer process within the thermal-hydraulics field. Previous research has predominantly focused on heat transfer tubes with large curvatures, resulting in experimental correlations that are largely limited to circular tubes and often neglect the effects of curvatures and inclinations on external condensation performance of tubes with limited curvatures or even flat plates. This study, conducted on the COAST (condensation and species transport) experimental facility, investigated steam condensation with non-condensable gases (NCGs) outside circular tubes/plates of different curvatures, covering a pressure range of 0.2∼1.6 MPa and an NCG concentration range of 7∼90%. The plate configurations included both upper-condensing plate and lower-condensing plate, with the influence of inclination angles also incorporated. The results show that the condensation heat transfer coefficient ( h c ) increases significantly with greater curvature, and the rate of this increase itself grows. The h c of the 100 mm tube shows an improvement of less than 10% compared to flat plate, whereas the 19 mm tube exhibits an average enhancement of approximately 50% compared to the 100 mm tube. Furthermore, the h c increases notably with decreasing inclination, although the magnitude of this improvement gradually diminishes. For the 19 mm tube, the h c of the horizontal tube is 18∼27% higher than that of the vertical tube. For the 100 mm tube, the improvement is only about 5∼15%. The influence of inclination angles on plate condensation differs from that on tubes. For upper-condensing plate, the h c is weaker in the horizontal orientation than in the vertical orientation. While that of the lower-condensing plate initially enlarges and then diminishes from horizontal to vertical orientation. Moreover, the h c of the lower-condensing plate consistently surpasses that of the upper plate. Finally, an experimental correlation applicable to heat transfer tubes and plates with different curvatures and inclination angles was developed. A comparison with existing correlations demonstrates that the proposed correlation has a predictive accuracy within ±20%.

title: High-throughput gamma-ray spectrometry using 1-GS/s current-pulse acquisition and FPGA-based cascaded pile-up recovery
abstract: Long decay tails introduced by charge-sensitive preamplifiers increase the probability of pulse pile-up and limit the output count rate of conventional gamma-ray spectrometers under high-count-rate conditions. This work presents a high-throughput gamma-ray spectrometer based on current-pulse readout, 1-GS/s waveform digitization, and field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based pile-up recovery. The 16-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) stream is processed using four parallel 250-MHz preprocessing lanes, event-driven variable-length packetization, dynamic allocation among eight first-in, first-out (FIFO)-backed recovery channels, and 16-stage cascaded template subtraction. The system was evaluated using a 1.5-inch LaBr 3 :Ce detector and a 137 Cs source. The measured single-pulse rise time and decay-time constant were 33 and 47 ns, respectively. For a representative isolated pulse, the normalized root-mean-square error relative to the average template was 0.0134. Noise-injection simulations yielded a standard deviation of 0.776 ns for timing deviations obtained using digital constant-fraction discrimination. For the investigated pulse separations and amplitude ratio, template-alignment errors between −3 and +3 ns resulted in a maximum absolute relative error below 1.8% in the mean recovered secondary-pulse amplitude. Using the estimated input rates, valid-event throughputs of 95.6% and 82.1% were obtained at 1 and 4.96 Mcps, respectively, with corresponding energy resolutions of 3.14% and 5.27% at 661.7 keV under their respective operating conditions. A system-level comparison showed that the proposed spectrometer maintained a more nearly linear input–output count-rate response and a smaller rate-dependent degradation in energy resolution than the conventional charge-sensitive configuration over the common measurement range.

title: Benchmarking CAPRIX pin behaviour under irradiation with high plutonium content: comparison with experimental data
abstract: This paper presents the results of the second phase of the benchmark exercise in the Plutonium Management for More Agility project (PuMMA), which aims to enhance the reliability of fuel performance codes (FPCs) for Mixed Oxide (MOX) fuels with high plutonium content. This phase involved the simulation of the CAPRIX irradiation (45% of Pu) carried out in the PHENIX reactor in France. Thirteen organizations from nine countries participated, using eight different fuel performance codes. In this phase, 7 codes then improved its modelling by optimizing parameters and/or improving the formulation of some models involved in the computation. A comparative analysis was then conducted between the codes and the post-irradiation experimental (PIE) results, with the objective of identifying the improvements made, the discrepancies still observed, and to define future areas for improvement and development. The present paper demonstrates the results for the CAPRIX pin. The main results despite the discrepancies noted between the codes and/or with the experimental data, the work carried out through this benchmark has demonstrated the capacity of the codes to optimise/improve their simulation in order to approximate the PIE. Moreover, the methodology employed yielded a comprehensive and precise analysis, thus facilitating the suggestion of approaches to the development of specific models. This finding thus demonstrates the potential of fuel performance codes modelling pins with high Pu contents.

title: Radiation dose analysis in the IR-IECF device: numerical analysis with geant4 simulation and experimental measurements
abstract: This study presents a combined experimental and Geant4-based assessment of the radiation field and shielding performance of the Iranian Inertial Electrostatic Confinement fusion device (IR-IECF) operating in deuterium–deuterium (D–D) mode and producing 2.45 MeV neutrons. A detailed Geant4 model of the IR-IECF device, its surrounding borated-polyethylene shielding, and the relevant dosimetry locations was developed to calculate neutron and gamma dose distributions. Experimental gamma doses were measured using GR-200 (LiF:Mg,Cu,P) thermoluminescent dosimeters, whereas neutron ambient dose-equivalent rates were measured using a Berthold LB6411 rem counter. In the Geant4 model, neutron dose scoring was performed using LiF-based virtual dosimeters positioned at the corresponding monitoring locations, allowing the numerical results to be compared with the experimental neutron measurements. The simulated neutron and gamma dose values showed good agreement with the corresponding experimental data, supporting the reliability of the developed Geant4 model for radiation-field characterization. In addition, a dedicated secondary-particle scoring analysis was performed to characterize the secondary radiation generated during neutron transport. Electrons, protons, and photons were the dominant recorded secondary particles, while secondary neutrons accounted for approximately 1.69% of the recorded secondary tracks. Overall, the combined experimental and numerical approach provides a practical framework for radiation-field characterization and shielding assessment of IECF-based neutron sources.

title: Multivariable control of large-scale pressurized water reactor based on LPV-MPC algorithm over a wide operating range
abstract: For energy conservation, large-scale Pressurized Water Reactors (PWRs) are required to participate in grid peak shaving. Compared to traditional PID control, Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithm offers advantages in handling multivariable control problems. However, PWR systems exhibit strong nonlinearity under wide-range operation, limiting conventional MPC performance. Therefore, Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) models, valued for their nonlinear approximation capability and low computational cost, are employed in nonlinear MPC. This paper proposes an LPV model-based MPC algorithm to enhance the control of a nonlinear HPR1000 model. An iterative optimization strategy is adopted for LPV model identification: first, initial local models are identified using the asymptotic method; then, parameters of the weighting functions are estimated via least squares; finally, the LPV model is optimized iteratively based on the total data. The local models demonstrate good performance in both time-domain and frequency-domain validation. The optimized LPV model shows high similarity to the plant’s step responses at both high and low loads, confirming its suitability for MPC controller. The LPV-MPC is compared with both the original control system and a fixed-model MPC (F-MPC) through test scenarios at 100 % and 50 % FP. The results indicate that the LPV-MPC controller offers comparable performance at 100 % FP, but exhibits faster regulation speed and stronger capability in suppressing SG water level fluctuations at 50 % FP. The comparison with F-MPC demonstrates that the LPV-MPC possesses stronger adaptability and robustness. Meanwhile, a large-scale transition scenario was implemented. The comparative analysis confirms that the LPV-MPC controller possesses superior load-following performance.

title: Safety Culture in Licensed Indonesian Irradiation Facilities: Evaluating Key Attributes Through the IAEA Harmonized Model
abstract: The growing deployment of industrial irradiation technology utilizing high-activity sealed sources and high-energy accelerators escalates radiological risks. Comprehensive safety culture evaluations are critical to prevent radiological consequences and maintain the credibility of the national nuclear safety infrastructure. This study assesses key attributes within licensed Indonesian irradiation facilities using the IAEA Harmonized Safety Culture Model, addressing the lack of empirical evidence in this sector. A quantitative, exploratory study was conducted across multiple organizational levels (operators, supervisors, management, HSE, and administrative personnel), yielding 39 respondents. The questionnaire evaluated 43 attributes grouped into ten IAEA-defined characteristics. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including frequency distributions, mean scores, and standard deviations, supported by validity and reliability testing of the instrument. Workplace communication, facilities reflect respect, learning from experience, training, and resolution emerged as relatively strengths; conversely, respect is evident, free flow of information, benchmarking, recognize and question assumptions, and question uncertainty were identified as priority areas for improvement. The findings provide an empirical baseline and context-specific insights for operators and regulators to strengthen targeted safety strategies. While exploratory and perception-based, this study establishes a foundation for progressive safety maturity. Future research should integrate objective safety performance indicators, larger datasets, and complementary qualitative approaches to systematically examine the causal relationships driving organizational safety performance.

title: A 2D Defense-in-Depth Waypoint Graph Framework for Evaluation of Physical Protection Systems at Research Reactors
abstract: Research reactors represent potential targets for sabotage scenarios with severe radiological consequences, requiring rigorous evaluation of the effectiveness of physical protection systems (PPSs). Traditional evaluation tools based on the Estimate of Adversary Sequence Interruption model and its extensions employ one-dimensional adversary sequence diagrams (ASDs) that abstract facility geometry into sequential protection layers, limiting the spatial analysis of alternative adversary routes. This study presents a two-dimensional waypoint graph framework for evaluating the effectiveness of PPSs. Facility layouts are represented as sparse waypoint graphs encoding spatial coordinates, probability of detection PD, and barrier delay times td, with adversary movement constrained by the progression of the defense-in-depth layer. A backward Dijkstra-based pathfinding formulation with exhaustive critical detection point enumeration is used to identify the most vulnerable path under a conservative adversary strategy, without relying on heuristic assumptions. The global pathfinding solution was independently verified through full enumeration of feasible adversary paths. A Monte Carlo simulation was integrated to quantify the influence of the detection probability variability on the probability of interruption distribution. A hypothetical research reactor case study demonstrates that the proposed framework identifies more vulnerable adversary paths than the ASD-based approach under equivalent spatial traversal conditions, resulting in probability of interruption PI values up to 4.25% lower under varying response force timing scenarios. The complete evaluation demonstrated computational tractability suitable for iterative PPS evaluation. Analysis of modified PPS configurations showed where the greatest vulnerability lies within the facility.

title: Parametric Study of Sn Electrorefining in a LiCl-KCl-CaCl2 Eutectic: A Surrogate System for Pu Electrorefining
abstract: Molten-salt electrorefining (ER) is essential for purifying chemically active metals, including plutonium, that cannot be processed in aqueous systems. However, systematic experimental studies linking operating parameters to ER performance and reliable process-monitoring criteria remain limited. In this work, tin–nickel (Sn-Ni) electrorefining in a LiCl-KCl-CaCl 2 eutectic is employed as a non-radioactive surrogate to investigate the effects of anode composition, temperature, and SnCl 2 seeding concentration. Kilogram-scale ER experiments were conducted using an automated operating protocol that monitored voltage, current, static refining resistance, and back-electromotive force (back-emf) as run termination indicators. Product yield, faradaic efficiency, and refined-metal purity were quantified through post-run mass balances and chemical analysis. All conditions produced refined Sn with ≥99.5 wt.% purity. Increasing SnCl 2 seeding concentration and operating temperature improved product yield, whereas increasing Ni impurity in the anode feed from 2 to 3 wt.% significantly reduced yield and faradaic efficiency. Comparison of monitoring metrics showed static refining resistance to be more consistent and reliable than back-emf for identifying run completion, as back-emf exhibited false positives and missed late-stage transitions. These results provide practical guidance for ER process control and reinforce the Sn-Ni system as a surrogate for molten-salt electrorefining of plutonium.

title: Gaussian Process Regression-Based Prediction of Spatial Source-Term Distributions in Activated Bioshield Concrete Using Limited Sampling Data
abstract: Reliable reconstruction of spatial source-term distributions is important for the radiological characterization of activated bioshield concrete during nuclear power plant decommissioning. Although full-field neutron transport calculations remain necessary, performing mesh-wise activation calculations or radiochemical analyses over an entire structure is computationally and practically demanding. This study developed a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) approach to reconstruct spatial source-term distributions from limited data. The OPR-1000 bioshield concrete region was discretized into 7,500 mesh cells, and reference specific-activity fields for Co-60, Eu-152, and U-234 were generated using MCNP6.3 and SCALE6.3/ORIGEN. Reconstruction performance was compared among a coordinate-only GPR (CO-GPR) using spatial coordinates, a flux-only log-linear regression (FO-LR) baseline, and a flux-informed GPR (FI-GPR) incorporating total neutron flux. CO-GPR reproduced the overall spatial trends but retained localized residual errors as the number of training points increased. FI-GPR reproduced the reference fields with 10–20 training points and reduced both average and maximum errors. It achieved lower errors than FO-LR for Eu-152 and U-234, while maintaining high accuracy for Co-60, demonstrating consistent reconstruction performance across the three radionuclides. It also yielded narrower GPR posterior prediction intervals associated with sparse-data reconstruction, although empirical coverage differed among the radionuclides. The proposed method therefore reduces the number of required mesh-wise ORIGEN calculations while retaining the full-field MCNP flux calculation.

title: Mechanical pump shaft seals: Dynamic stability and dynamic sealing considerations
abstract: The majority of power reactor designs utilize pumps to circulate the primary coolant past the fuel to transfer heat away and provide the thermal power to generate electricity. Mechanical shaft seals are critical nuclear components used to prevent leakage between a rotating pump shaft and the stationary housing for the pump. Success is usually achieved by finding the right balance of providing sufficient leakage to lubricate the seal, without overwhelming the collection system. Mechanical pump seals have two lapped-flat faces in close proximity, one rotating and the other stationary, across which a small amount of leakage (lubricant) is driven by the pressure being sealed (hydrostatic seals) or leakage is driven by the shaft rotation (hydrodynamic seals). This paper will discuss design aspects associated with hydrostatic seals. The gap between these seal faces can change over operation due to intermittent rubbing from loss of film uniformity as a result of: shaft tilt, eccentricity, misalignment, elastomeric seal friction, and vibration. This intermittent rubbing can cause a loss of the initial convergence set during manufacturing, which can cause unstable dynamic response, such as hard rubbing (unlubricated seal face operation). Additionally, this paper will discuss considerations related to the design of dynamic elastomeric seals, which observe the same shaft operating challenges, but also need to move along the shaft without affecting the lubricating film.

title: Finite element model updating of building structures under seismic excitation: A parallelized latent space-based Bayesian framework
abstract: Enhancing seismic fragility and risk assessment of nuclear power plants relies on accurate prediction of reactor building responses to seismic hazards, which can be further improved through dynamic analysis of high-fidelity finite element (FE) models. However, FE models often exhibit non-negligible discrepancies from actual structures due to various sources of uncertainty, necessitating FE model updating with rigorous quantification of associated uncertainties. This paper presents a GPU-accelerated latent space-based Bayesian framework for FE model updating of building structures. In the proposed framework, high-dimensional structural response data (e.g., time histories or frequency response functions) are projected into a low-dimensional latent space using a multimodal variational autoencoder (MVAE), thereby enabling efficient and tractable likelihood evaluation without explicit modeling in the original observation space. Once trained, the surrogate enables amortized inference, allowing posterior sampling to be performed without additional simulator evaluations. We specifically employ a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) sampler, whose population-based formulation allows parallel evaluation of the approximate likelihood on GPUs, resulting in computational efficiency and robustness against multimodal and complex posterior distributions. The proposed framework is evaluated through numerical benchmarking using a shear-type building structure with a multimodal posterior distribution. The results indicate that the proposed approach can recover the major posterior modes while achieving efficient inference through GPU-based parallel evaluation. We further apply the framework to experimental data from a shaking table test of a reinforced concrete building structure. The results suggest that the inferred posterior distributions and posterior predictive responses are consistent with the observed data, even in the presence of sparse observations that induce complex posterior distributions.

title: Reliability assessment of nuclear powered zero-liquid-discharge cogeneration systems with thermal energy storage
abstract: Nuclear power has the potential to simultaneously address demand for clean electricity, freshwater scarcity, and demand for valuable minerals, such as lithium, if it is thermally integrated with zero liquid discharge desalination (ZLD). ZLD is an energy-intensive process that desalinates seawater, mining its minerals and extracting freshwater such that no liquid is discharged. However, such nuclear-thermal integration could present challenges for the reliability of the combined system, given both nuclear and desalination are capital-intensive technologies. In this paper, the reliability of such a system is assessed for different maintenance strategies. Additionally, the impact of using thermal energy storage (TES) to decouple designs to maintain thermal independence and reduce downtime is investigated. The system is modeled in Event Modeling Risk Assessment using Linked Diagrams (EMRALD). We determined that performing preventative maintenance on degrading system components can reduce reactor downtime by as much as 40% and that introducing TES to decouple the power cycle from the ZLD reduces reactor downtime by as much as 65%. The impact of decoupling on reducing reactor downtime was found to depend on the component failure rates of the ZLD system, with such a strategy being less impactful for a higher reliability process heat application. High component reliabilities in the TES were found to be necessary to prevent increased downtime in the ZLD system, as failure in the TES could otherwise drive the ZLD system offline. Seeing these changes in system performance, this research shows how EMRALD can be used to compare the reliabilities of different cogenerating plant designs and maintenance strategies.

title: Numerical investigations on heat transfer characteristics and melting behaviour of a PHWR pressure tube under combined LOCA and moderator voiding
abstract: Failure of the Pressure tube under severe Loss of Coolant Accident (LOCA) with Emergency Core Cooling System (ECCS) failure and complete moderator voiding is a serious issue in Indian Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (IPHWRs). The present study investigates the thermal behaviour, heat transfer characteristics, and melting progression of a single fuel channel of the 220 MWe IPHWR using ANSYS 2023 R1. The steady-state simulations were performed for heat fluxes ranging from 900 to 4950 W/m 2 to determine the temperature distributions and to identify the melting initiation heat flux for the onset of melting, while the heat flux ranges 4400–4950 W/m 2 were used for the transient phase change simulations to determine the melting rate. The results show that there is a significant temperature asymmetry within the pressure tube-calandria tube assembly. The peak temperature of the pressure tube was raised from 396.25°C to 2080.60°C and the melting initiation heat flux was predicted to be approximately 4400 W/m 2 . With increasing heat flux, the complete melting time decreased from 80 s to 8 s, with an increase of about ten in the Melting Rate Index (MRI), thus representing very non-linear melting behaviour. The proposed PT-CT Thermal Coupling Index (TCI), Normalized Temperature Ratio (NTR) and Melting Rate Index (MRI) are quantitative assessments of the thermal vulnerability and melting progress. The proposed approach will be useful for severe accident analysis and safety assessment of Indian PHWR systems for engineering applications.

title: Nuclear ship Mutsu and the 1974 radiation leak Incident: Technical background and management lessons
abstract: During its experimental voyage in September 1974, Japan’s first nuclear-powered ship, Mutsu, experienced abnormal radiation during a low-power reactor test conducted approximately 800 km east of Cape Shiriya in Aomori Prefecture. The immediate technical mechanism involved fast-neutron streaming and secondary gamma-ray generation caused by an inadequate shielding configuration. Although the event did not involve major fuel damage or a large release of radioactive material, it developed into a serious operational and political problem, leading to resistance to the ship’s return and to a government investigation. This paper reconstructs the incident and reviews the technical and organizational conditions that shaped its occurrence and subsequent handling. Drawing on official reports, technical records, and prior studies, it examines how inadequate project integration, limited design review, contractual separation, and communication failures complicated what began as a shielding-design problem. Using action system theory of management as a heuristic framework, we organize key task-level findings and relate them to recurrent patterns in major public technology projects. The case indicates that, in prototype nuclear systems, technical adequacy alone is insufficient: integrated review, clear responsibility, and effective communication are also essential to safe development and testing.

title: Nuclear reactor cladding enhancement via magnetron sputtering: Examining the effects of increasing Mo content in high-entropy coating on Zircaloy-4
abstract: Single-metal interlayer coating systems reliably protect standard Zircaloy tubes, making them suitable candidates for accident-tolerant fuel (ATF) cladding in nuclear service environments. However, they also deplete during interfacial metallic interactions (e.g., during Nb-Zr interdiffusion) and co-precipitate (e.g., when Mo interlays between Cr and Zr), thereby losing their availability as protective coatings for long-term use. In the quest to address these shortcomings, the present study explores a multiple-metal-engineered high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating (CrFeNiMoAl), proposed as a reliable alternative, particularly based on Mo as a refractory metal, for testing under high-thermal conditions. Four coating variants with Mo content ranging from 0 to 30 % (HEAMo0-3) were deposited on Zircaloy-4 via magnetron sputtering. To examine their corrosion behavior, these coatings were comparatively tested under conditions simulating Pressurized Water Reactor (PWR) cooling systems via electrochemistry in LiOH/H 3 BO 3 , by accelerated annealing (1200 °C at atmospheric pressure for 5 min), and subcritical corrosion tests at 360 °C in 18.6 MPa steam. In addition to material strengthening, improved barrier performance is attributed to the optimal Mo content, which supports the presence of predominantly body-centered cubic (BCC) nanocrystalline multiphase structure. Barrier performance depends largely on Mo content in the following order of increasing strengths: HEAMo1 (with 10.1 % Mo) ˃ HEAMo2 (with 20.7 % Mo) ˃ HEAMo3 (with 30 % Mo) ˃ HEAMo0 (with 0 % Mo). Higher Mo content oversaturated the internal coating structure, leading to coating degradation, increased Mo-ion release, and the formation of additional pathways for corrosive ions to reach the Zr surface. This work does not aim to investigate interfacial elemental diffusion, as ample research already addresses this topic. The essential insight from the present study concerns the impact of coolant chemistry and coating content on the performance and durability of ATF-cladding materials for next-generation nuclear reactor fuel systems.

title: Modeling (α,n) neutron source terms in the ALEPH depletion code
abstract: The modeling of ( α ,n) neutron source terms in the ALEPH depletion code is assessed for two contrasting systems: spent nuclear fuel, a heavy actinide-oxide matrix, and an americium-beryllium (AmBe) source, a light low-Z matrix. In each, the source intensity and alpha spectrum are computed both by the analytic thick target yield and by direct alpha transport. For the spent fuel the yield from MCNP, ALEPH’s transport solver, falls 16% below the thick target yield, whereas for AmBe the two agree to within about 1%. The discrepancy is traced to MCNP’s internal stopping power table, which deviates from the validated SRIM and NIST ASTAR data in the heavy matrix but not the light one. The thick target yield is therefore at present the only reliable route to ( α ,n) source terms within ALEPH: MCNP alpha transport should not be used in heavy matrices, and an explicit transport estimate should come from a code with validated stopping powers, such as PHITS. A separate, matrix-independent energy-binning artifact in the MCNP alpha fluence spectrum is also identified; it redistributes fluence between neighboring bins without biasing integral quantities, and matters only when a differential spectrum is tallied. The neutron emission spectra from JENDL-5, JEFF-4.0 and TENDL-2025 are assessed through their effect on the ambient dose equivalent rate H*(10), computed for the AmBe source in a PHITS model of a shielded calibration laboratory and benchmarked against the reference ISO 8529-1 spectrum. The comparison supports JENDL-5 as the ALEPH default.

title: Interfacial dissolution behavior of UO2 in carbonate-based groundwater environments
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the dissolution behavior of UO 2 in carbonate-bearing groundwater is critical for predicting the long-term release of uranium from spent nuclear fuel in geological disposal environments. This study investigates the pH-dependent interfacial dissolution of UO 2 in these environments to identify distinct reaction regimes governed by surface chemistry. Two uranium oxide models with contrasting structural characteristics were examined: structurally disordered electrodeposited UO 2+x films and well-crystallized sintered UO 2 pellets exhibiting terrace-step morphologies. Dissolution processes were monitored using a combination of quartz crystal microbalance (QCM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), Raman spectroscopy, and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Both materials exhibit consistent biphasic dissolution kinetics, characterized by an initial rapid uranium release followed by a slower, steady-state regime. Dissolution is accelerated under mildly acidic carbonate conditions (pH 6.0) and suppressed under highly alkaline conditions (pH 12.0). Under representative groundwater conditions (pH 8.0), the UO 2 surface develops a relatively stable interfacial layer involving partial oxidation and surface-bound carbonates. These findings demonstrate that pH-controlled interfacial chemistry and initial defect density fundamentally dictate uranium dissolution, providing critical mechanistic insights for predicting radionuclide release in deep geological repositories.

title: Health risk and dominant factors of indoor radon concentrations in Souq Al-Khamees and Ka'am, Libya
abstract: This study assessed indoor 222Rn concentrations and their determinants in Souq Al-Khamees and Ka’am, Libya, to quantify public health risks and identify mitigation strategies. Passive dosimeters were deployed in 55 dwellings for 90 days. Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) with advanced feature engineering analyzed 17 variables, including functional transformations. Arithmetic Mean (AM) concentrations were 77 Bq/m³ in Souq Al-Khamees and 116 Bq/m³ in Ka’am. While geometric means (39 and 44 Bq/m³) reflect a stable regional background, WHO reference level exceedance rates reached 18.4% and 21.3%, respectively. The MLR model (R² = 0.692) identified the reciprocals of modified ventilation (1/(V+2)) and storey level (1/(S+2)) as the primary significant predictors. To address single-season sampling bias (March–June), a regional Mediterranean seasonal correction factor of 1.29 was integrated, showing that true annual exposures, Annual Effective Dose Equivalents (AEDE), and lifetime health risks exceed measured seasonal parameters. Consequently, 222Rn exposure increases estimated lifetime lung cancer risk for never-smokers to 16 and 20 per 1,000, respectively, escalating synergistically to 276 and 352 per 1,000 for current smokers. Increasing daily ventilation past 2–4 hours provides a critical, cost-effective regional mitigation strategy.

title: Characterisation of Annular UO2 Pellets Fabricated Using Spark Plasma Sintering and Conventional Sintering
abstract: Internally and EXternally cooled Annular Fuel (IXAF) is a novel nuclear fuel concept that is being researched due to several advantages such as enhanced heat transfer, lower Peak Fuel Temperature (PFT), and lower fission gas release. The fuel concept has gained some momentum recently due to its enhanced accident tolerance. In this study the fabrication of IXAF by two different processing routes are compared. Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) is a novel powder consolidation technique with good near net shaping ability as compared to Conventional Sintering (CS). This publication compares the results obtained from the characterisation of annular pellets fabricated from Spark Plasma Sintering to that from conventional sintering. The as-sintered pellets were characterised to compare their densities, dimensional change, microstructure, and grain size. The internal diameter of the as-sintered pellets was measured by a novel replicate technique and compared. Unexpectedly, the SPS technique proved to be a less viable alternative to CS in improving the near net shaping of the IXAF.

title: Catalyzed deuterium fusion neutron source for the transmutation of minor actinides, production of tritium, and electrical power generation
abstract: The accumulated inventory of spent nuclear fuel in the United States exceeds 90,000 metric tons, with long-term radiological hazards dominated by minor actinides that require isolation for thousands of years. This study details a possible solution to these challenges that also provides significant electrical power. The method employs a fusion system operating in catalyzed deuterium (Cat-D) mode producing the high neutron flux required for this task. It is based on the Compact Field Reversed Configuration Fusion Reactor (CFR2), where the plasma is sequentially compressed to fusion conditions remote from the burn chamber and then translated into the chamber surrounded by the fission blanket. A Monte Carlo neutronics analysis of a subcritical actinide transmutation blanket and the design was optimized. The optimized blanket employs FLiNaK eutectic fluoride salt enriched to 90% 6 Li and containing 17.53 mol% transuranic fluorides as the combined coolant, moderator, and fissile medium. The design achieves keff=0.9695 with a blanket volume of 13.4 m 3 . The FRC is pulsed at 4Hz with a tritium fraction of 4%, yielding a neutron flux of 4×10 18 n/s. This fission system burns 683 kg/yr of TRU, produces 9.6 kg/yr of tritium and 1,431 MWth, requiring only 17.5 MWe to power the CFR2.

title: Numerical simulation and validation of submerged isothermal liquid metal jets
abstract: A key phenomenon under examination in liquid metal (LM) cooled nuclear reactors is the formation and evolution of submerged, axisymmetric, round LM jets in the upper plenum region, with particular emphasis on the influence of geometric configuration and density stratification on the development and stability of these flow structures. Experimentally, characterization of the optically opaque LM flow fields is performed using ultrasonic Doppler velocimetry (UDV). The primary objective of this study is to employ existing experimental data to validate computational models that can subsequently be used as predictive tools for simulating other LM coolant applications. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) software, the evolution of neutrally buoyant jets is analyzed and compared against theoretical descriptions. Unobstructed and obstructed inlet configurations are investigated over a range of injection flow rates and assessed relative to classical free-shear round jet theory. A modified k– ɛ turbulence model, with coefficients specifically calibrated for axisymmetric jet flows, is applied to characterize the behavior of confined pipe jets and obstructed LM jets over a range of inlet conditions, yielding results consistent with established empirical pipe jet correlations. For the Gallium Thermal–hydraulic Experiment (GaTE), good agreement between CFD predictions and theoretical expectations was obtained when reduced effective inlet diameters were adopted, as opposed to the assumptions of isothermal, unconfined round jet theory in an infinite domain. CFD models for obstructed jet flow were further validated experimentally in the presence of the upper internal structure (UIS) of the GaTE facility, with agreement demonstrated against the available experimental velocity measurements. The mean relative deviation between the experimental and computational results is determined to be less than 15%.

title: Effect of geometric protrusions and depressions on critical heat flux density of the heating surface
abstract: In the “Melted Reactor Retention and External Pressure Vessel Cooling (IVR-ERVC)” strategy for nuclear power plants, the Critical Heat Flux (CHF) serves as the critical limit for ensuring pressure vessel integrity. Traditional safety assessment procedures rely on an ideal flat surface assumption, neglecting macroscopic irregularities caused by corrosion and manufacturing defects during long-term operation. To address this issue, this study systematically investigated the impact mechanism of macroscopic irregularities on CHF using a self-developed saturated pool boiling experimental system and high-speed imaging technology. Results demonstrate that as the system approaches boiling crisis, macroscopic convex and concave defects reduce average CHF by approximately 27.4% and 16.7%, respectively. Mechanism analysis demonstrates that concave defects form a “steam trap, ”the vapor retention is attributed primarily to triple-phase contact line (TPL) pinning at the sharp machined edges, leading to bubble retention and localized drying; whereas convex defects impede bubble detachment through “mechanical obstruction,” resulting in premature CHF. Once validated under conditions more representative of IVR-ERVC, a “surface degradation penalty coefficient” may be considered in future nuclear safety analyses as a possible conservative option.

title: Counterpart test for LSTF SBLOCA at the RPV upper head using ATLAS test facility
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the OECD-ATLAS2 B5.1 test, the counterpart for the LSTF SB-PV-07 test. This test simulates a 1% small-break loss-of-coolant accident (SBLOCA) with the break at the reactor pressure vessel (RPV) upper head. The transient scenario considered a total failure of the high-pressure injection (HPI) system. But it incorporated the accident management (AM) actions to mitigate the accident and considered the inflow of non-condensable nitrogen gas from the accumulators following coolant depletion of accumulator (ACC). This test scenario is distinguished by its complex coolant distribution and depressurization characteristics compared to typical cold-leg break accident. This test was designed to investigate the thermal–hydraulic response of the ATLAS (Advanced Thermal-hydraulic Test Loop for Accident Simulation) facility compared to the LSTF test result. In addition to that, the effectiveness of the accident management actions considered in this test scenario was another objective of this study. From the test results, the ATLAS facility successfully reproduced the essential thermal–hydraulic phenomena that can be expected in the SBLOCA conditions including loop seal clearing (LSC) and core heat-up even though several differences were found with the LSTF test result. Critically, the study demonstrated that manual accident management actions − comprising manual HPI actuation and rapid secondary-side depressurization − effectively mitigated the accident progression and cooled down the system successfully even under the influence of non-condensable gases.

title: A note on neutron point kinetics with delayed neutrons and prompt neutrons as separate populations
abstract: This note describes the development of a theory of point kinetics with delayed neutrons and prompt neutrons as separated populations. The separated point kinetics are demonstrated to be consistent with the original point kinetics, and are used in three novel applications to: (1) visualise the separate evolution timescales of the two neutron populations, (2) allow us to comment quantitatively on the ‘delayed neutron fraction’ versus ’relative yield’ definitions of the parameter β in favour of the latter, and (3) suggest a possible deficiency that the use of reactivity as a parameter may not be able to accurately model the true physical effects of perturbations to fission production.

title: Radiological characterization for research reactor decommissioning: Application of lessons learned from the VVR-S reactor to the WWR-M facility
abstract: Radiological characterization is a key element of the decommissioning of any nuclear facility, providing the information required for dismantling planning, radiation protection, radioactive waste management, and final site release. This paper presents a characterization strategy developed for the decommissioning of the WWR-M research reactor in Ukraine, integrating historical records, radiological surveys, in situ measurements, laboratory analyses, activation assessments, and radionuclide inventory determination. The proposed approach covers three main stages of decommissioning: dismantling, radioactive waste management, and final cleaning of premises. Particular attention is given to the characterization of activated structures, contaminated systems and components, radioactive waste streams, and residual contamination in building materials. The methodology incorporates lessons learned from the successful decommissioning of the VVR-S research reactor in Romania, including activation assessment, dose-rate mapping, radionuclide inventory determination, and waste classification. By combining direct measurements with analytical and modelling techniques, the proposed program provides the information necessary for safe and efficient decommissioning implementation while reducing uncertainties and optimizing characterization efforts. The approach may serve as a practical framework for other research reactors undergoing decommissioning.

title: Coriolis Force and Inclination Angle Influences of MHD Flow Over a Spinning Plate Using bvp4c and ANN Prediction
abstract: Rotating heat-exchanger surfaces, disc-type cooling systems, and inclined rotating machinery in industrial processes require accurate prediction of heat and mass transfer under combined electromagnetic and rotational effects, a problem that has not previously been addressed in a single unified model together with a fast prediction tool. This study investigates the electro-magnetohydrodynamic flow of a rotating Newtonian nanofluid over an inclined, spinning stretching sheet, incorporating Coriolis force, Lorentz force, viscous dissipation, Joule heating, and a heat source/sink, together with Brownian motion and thermophoresis. This combination of effects is directly representative of rotating heat-exchanger and disc-cooling configurations, where inclination and rotation act simultaneously and cannot be modeled independently. Coriolis force and the surface inclination angle are incorporated into the Navier–Stokes equations governing the flow, and the resulting system of partial differential equations is reduced, via a suitable similarity transformation, to a system of ordinary differential equations, which is solved using the bvp4c solver in MATLAB. The adaptability, robustness, and precision of this method make it an effective tool for addressing such fluid-flow problems. The effects of the Coriolis force, surface inclination angle, heat generation, Prandtl number, and Grashof number on the temperature, concentration, and velocity fields are examined in detail. The present results show highly satisfactory agreement with existing published results. The numerical (bvp4c) results are further used to train an artificial neural network (ANN) model, enabling near-instant prediction of key engineering quantities—skin friction, Nusselt number, and Sherwood number without repeated numerical solution of the governing equations; the ANN predictions show excellent agreement with the bvp4c results. The findings of this study are directly applicable to the design of cooling systems for large industrial machinery and consumer electronics such as laptops and cellphones, as well as to rotating heat-exchanger and disc-cleaning applications, food processing, and other rotating-machinery systems where nanofluid-based cooling is employed.

title: Trap-Assisted Carrier Loss and Transient Signal Degradation in Diamond Radiation Detectors
abstract: Diamond radiation detectors are promising for neutron and charged-particle detection owing to their radiation hardness, fast charge collection, and stability in harsh environments. However, traps introduced during growth, fabrication, irradiation, or long-term operation can act as trapping and recombination centers, causing transient signal degradation that remains insufficiently quantified. This work incorporates traps into an SRIM–TCAD–Garfield++ multi-physics framework to model trap-driven degradation in planar diamond detectors. The framework couples charged-particle energy deposition, electric-field-dependent carrier transport, trap-assisted capture and recombination, and Shockley–Ramo-induced current calculation. Furthermore, we construct an effective-lifetime model to evaluate effects of trap concentration, capture cross-section, and bias voltage. Results show that a strong-capture trap causes the transient response to evolve from a plateau-like waveform into a spike-like waveform as its concentration increases from 0.1 to 1000 ppm, decreasing signal duration from ∼9 ns to 0.5 ns. In contrast, a weak-capture trap barely distorts waveform collapse over the same concentration range, indicating trap density alone cannot determine signal degradation. Increasing the applied bias partially compensates for carrier loss by shortening transit time and suppressing diffusion, but this compensation becomes limited when trapping dominates. These results guide trap tolerance evaluation and bias optimization in diamond radiation detectors.

title: Assessment of sensitivity methodologies for a pressurized and depressurized loss of forced cooling in the high temperature gas-cooled test reactor
abstract: The goal of this study is to perform a preliminary assessment of loss of forced cooling events in the High Temperature Gas-cooled Test Reactor (HTGR-TR). This assessment is a demonstration of a sensitivity analysis framework that can be readily built upon. The framework employed two different sensitivity methodologies to highlight the necessity and benefits of including multiple metrics by comparing the predicted coefficients. An analysis will be performed for both a pressurized loss of forced cooling (PLOFC) and a depressurized loss of forced cooling (DLOFC). In both cases, the study will include the subsequent conduction cooldown in the reactor core. In particular, we will focus on a small, non-exhaustive, group of thermal properties within the HTGR-TR. The sensitivity study was used to exemplify how the framework can help determine which thermal properties have the most impact on the transient peak fuel temperature and 8-day (“late stage”) coolant outlet temperature. This study will include the calculation of both non-variance-based sensitivity coefficients and moment-independent Delta indices through the use of Monte Carlo sampling to compare the findings of both methodologies. An envelope of predicted fuel temperatures was generated through the sampling of the parameters during the sensitivity study. A peak fuel temperature of approximately 1500 K was predicted for both the PLOFC and DLOFC. The peak temperature was dominated by steady-state conditions, resulting in the same peak temperature for both transients. After the onset of both transients, a subsequent peak temperature was observed to be 1300 K for the PLOFC and 1400 K for the DLOFC. The fuel temperature did not exceed the steady-state temperatures during either transient. In both the PLOFC and DLOFC, the coolant inlet temperature and thermal conductivity were identified as most important for the transient fuel temperature. The Delta indices also identified these parameters as important with respect to the transient fuel temperature distribution. For example, the thermal conductivity had a Delta index of 0.28 and 0.5 for the PLOFC and DLOFC, respectively. In addition, an analysis of the 8-day coolant outlet temperature indicated a shift in parameter importance between the PLOFC and DLOFC with respect to nominal coolant pressure and moderator thermal conductivity. For example, a vastly differing Delta index of 0.1 and 0.7 was computed for the thermal conductivity during PLOFC and DLOFC, respectively. Discrepancies between the sensitivity studies highlight the potential strengths and weaknesses of different sensitivity approaches, emphasizing the value of including different methodologies during sensitivity analyses.
title_ko: 고온 가스 냉각 시험 원자로에서 강제 냉각의 가압 및 감압 손실에 대한 감도 방법론 평가

title: Neutron activation analysis at the Moroccan TRIGA MARK II reactor: state of the art, methodological advances, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Neutron Activation Analysis (NAA) is a powerful nuclear analytical technique widely used for multi-elemental characterization due to its high sensitivity, accuracy, and non-destructive nature. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of studies conducted at the Moroccan TRIGA MARK II research reactor (CNESTEN), highlighting the applications and methodological advances of Instrumental Neutron Activation Analysis (INAA). Environmental monitoring, food safety, medicinal plant analysis, and geochemical investigations emerge as the main application domains. The implementation of the k 0 -standardization method has significantly improved analytical performance and reproducibility. In parallel, the development of Prompt Gamma Neutron Activation Analysis (PGNAA), currently in a simulation-based phase, is discussed as a strategic extension of analytical capabilities. The integration of INAA and PGNAA is expected to enable a complementary analytical platform for both trace-level and real-time bulk analysis.

title: Measurement of the Zr-90(n, 2n) Zr-89 reaction cross section using fast neutron spectrum at the Tehran Research reactor (TRR)
abstract: Accurate determination of threshold neutron-induced reaction cross sections at relatively high threshold energies is of fundamental importance for nuclear model development and practical applications in physics. In addition, the evaluation and re-evaluation of such cross sections are relevant to ongoing efforts to improve the prompt fission neutron spectra of U-235 and U-238 within the IAEA CIELO project. In this work, the reaction cross sections of natural zirconium isotopes were investigated, with particular emphasis on the threshold reaction Zr-90(n,2n) Zr-89, which has a threshold energy above 10 MeV, in the neutron spectrum of the Tehran Research Reactor. Zirconium and monitor foils were irradiated in an irradiation box located in the reactor core. After an appropriate cooling period, the induced activities of the irradiated samples were measured using a high-purity germanium detector. To accurately estimate the neutron flux on the foils, the reactor core was modeled using the MCNPX code while accounting for burnup effects. The calculated foil reaction rates were then compared with the experimental values to validate the computed neutron flux. The spectrum-averaged cross section of the Zr-90(n,2n) Zr-89 reaction was measured to be 1.73 × 10 −5 barn with an uncertainty of 11%. The corresponding spectrum-averaged cross sections for the Zr-94(n,γ) Zr-95 and Zr-96(n,γ)Zr-97 reactions were 4.18 × 10 −2 and 8.04 × 10 −2 barn, respectively.

title: Experimental investigation of central blockages in a narrow rectangular channel using PIV: comparative study of square and diamond blockages
abstract: This study investigates the flow characteristics in a rectangular channel with center square and diamond blockages ( α =30%) at varying Reynolds numbers ( Re = 1268 – 4438) using particle image velocimetry (PIV). Time-averaged analysis, turbulence statistics, and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) were employed to examine the effects of blockage geometry on vortex evolution and turbulent kinetic energy dissipation. Key findings demonstrate that the diamond blockage induces localized high-vorticity zones due to its sharp vertices, resulting in stronger vortex cores. In contrast, the square blockage triggers flow stagnation due to its right-angled geometry, exhibiting broader turbulent kinetic energy dissipation and imposing stronger disturbances on the wake fluid. POD analysis and flow field reconstruction confirm the periodic vortex shedding in both blockage conditions. The present results can provide effective experimental data for blockage accident simulations of plate-type fuel assemblies.
title_ko: PIV를 이용한 좁은 직사각형 통로의 중심 막힘에 대한 실험적 조사: 사각형 및 다이아몬드 막힘에 대한 비교 연구

title: Enabling long-cycle, high-burnup light water SMRs with LEU+ fuel: A coupled core and fuel performance comparison of boron free and borated designs
abstract: Recent development of the LEU+ fuel supply chain enables new pathways to extend discharge burnup in light water SMRs, whose burnup is often reactivity-limited due to high neutron leakage. This study investigates LEU+ fueled core concepts for an i-SMR-based SMR with the objective of reducing annual spent fuel assembly discharge by approximately 30 % relative to the reference i-SMR with U-235 enrichment below 5 %, which corresponds to extending the cycle length from 730 to 1043 EFPD while maintaining the same number of feed fuel assemblies. Two variants are designed and assessed: a soluble-boron-free (SBF) core and a soluble-boron-used (SBU) core. For the SBF design, increased reliance on burnable absorbers and control rods motivates adoption of a 17 × 17 assembly with 28 guide tubes and 1 instrumentation tube, together with multiple IGD absorber options including enriched gadolinium configurations. Although a carefully designed shuffling scheme in the SBF core can effectively mitigate hoop stresses, control rod-driven axial depletion non-uniformity increases the peak nodal burnup to 80 MWd/kgU at rod average burnup below 65 MWd/kgU, accelerating fission gas release and rod internal pressure at high local burnup. In the SBU design, soluble boron provides cycle-long global reactivity control, reducing reliance on control rod insertion, yielding more uniform depletion behavior with moderated peak nodal burnup and fuel performance trends. Overall, the results support the technical viability of LEU+ for long-cycle SMR from the standpoint of neutronics and fuel performance under normal operation; however, the SBF implementation may induce increasing control rod-induced depletion non-uniformity when pursuing additional burnup extension beyond the burnup levels evaluated in this study (65 MWd/kgU).
title_ko: LEU + 연료로 장주기, 고연소 경수 SMR 활성화: 붕소 무함유 및 붕소 설계의 결합 코어 및 연료 성능 비교

title: A Geant4 based study of the response of surface barrier detector for alpha-particles
abstract: This study presents a Geant4 based comprehensive characterization of a silicon Surface Barrier Detector (SBD) for charged particle spectroscopy, with a specific focus on alpha particle detection. This work investigates the fundamental properties governing detector response, including the Bragg curve, Range and absolute detection efficiency. The Geant4 simulated Bragg curves have been found in good agreement with the corresponding TCAD-SRIM based data. For the 1–10 MeV domain of energy values of α-Particles, the Range in Silicon is found to exhibit a quadratic behavior. The Geant4 simulated absolute efficiency of SBD in parallel, coaxial source–detector configuration has been found in agreement with the corresponding experimental data. The Geant4 simulated absolute efficiency data has also been found in good agreement with the corresponding numerical/theoretical values for various values of source dimensions and for various values of source-to-detector axial distances. The Geant4 based absolute efficiency values show a gradual decrease with increasing radial displacement for fixed value of axial distance.

title: High-energy field-of-view completion in dual-source dual-energy CT using measurement-conditioned frequency-decoupled learning
abstract: This study proposes a measurement-conditioned framework for high-energy field-of-view (FOV) completion in dual-source dual-energy computed tomography (DECT). The model uses a full-FOV low-energy image, a measured central high-energy seed, and its support mask, while hard data consistency preserves the measured seed. A frequency-decoupled objective combines image-domain reconstruction, high-frequency adversarial supervision, and wavelet-based low-frequency attenuation constraints. Because true high-energy references are unavailable outside the physical high-energy FOV, a controlled seed–halo setting was used by withholding an annular region within the measured FOV for paired supervision and evaluation. Leave-one-patient-out experiments were conducted on thoracoabdominal DECT data from three patients. In the held-out halo, the proposed method achieved the lowest MAE and RMSE of 28.56 ± 6.23 HU and 40.86 ± 8.32 HU, respectively, and the highest SSIM of 0.9420 ± 0.0220 among the evaluated methods. It also more closely reproduced tissue-specific HU values and local intensity variation. In virtual monoenergetic imaging, it achieved the lowest MAE at all evaluated energies. Although true outer-FOV accuracy could not be directly validated, the results support the feasibility of the proposed approach for high-energy FOV completion and downstream spectral imaging.

title: Onset of flooding data at variable pressure in a large diameter tube for air-water and saturated steam-water fluid pairs
abstract: An experimental investigation to acquire flooding data for steam-water and air-water fluid pairs in a large-diameter vertical tube at above-atmospheric pressures has been conducted. The experimental program presented herein is the first to use a single test section with controlled boundary conditions for these pairs in a large-diameter vertical tube, enabling consistent comparisons of flooding characteristics. Many data exist for air-water flooding in annular flow within a large-diameter vertical tube and at various pressures. Steam-water flows are of interest for reactor applications, but insufficient data are available to enable reliable analysis. Evaluation of the effect of the fluid pair is performed to understand the applicability of the air-water data to steam-water applications. The pressure range was investigated by obtaining data at nominal pressures of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 MPa (0, 15, 30 and 45 psig) for air-water and steam-water flow conditions. Water subcooling was minimized to the extent possible in the steam-water tests to reduce the effect of phase change and permit a more level comparison with the air-water data. All data reported herein were taken at the onset of flooding, that is, conditions when flow reversal of the liquid phase first occurs. Flooding characteristics are presented in terms of the dimensionless Kutateladze parameter. The saturated steam-water flooding data over the pressure range closely trend with the air-water data.
title_ko: 공기-물 및 포화 증기-물 유체 쌍에 대한 대직경 튜브의 가변 압력에서 홍수 데이터의 시작

title: The effect of pulsating liquid sodium coolant inlets on flow structures and thermal mixing in a T-junction
abstract: Mixing of two pipe streams at different temperatures features in the secondary circuit of compact sodium-cooled fast reactors. This study presents the numerical simulation of flow features and mixing characteristics in the T-junction with the inlets subjected to co-pulsating and out-of-phase pulsating flows over a 4-s flow cycle. The main and branch pipe inlets are subjected to sine-sine and sine-cosine velocity variations. The momentum ratio is constant (3.57) in the first case, but varies between 1.73 and 7.38 in the second. The velocity magnitude profile in both cases gradually recovers to its pre-mixing shape after the T-junction; however, the profiles differ between the two half-cycles in Case 2. Turbulence intensity varied more in the upper part than in the lower part of the main pipe. The 90 o out-of-phase pulsating flow at the inlet resulted in increased temperature and turbulence intensity fluctuations along the flow axis. Momentum interactions dominate thermal mixing in the upper part of the pipe, while the lower half is dominated by gradual convection in the shear layers. The lower temperature mixing degree in 75% of the flow cross-section and 20% reduction in the temperature difference at the outlet show that more thermal mixing was achieved in Case 2. The 90° out-of-phase difference between the mixing inlets also causes the position of the thermal fluctuation to be momentarily away from the wall, which has implications for the extent of damage expected at the junction.
title_ko: T-접합부에서 액체 소듐 냉각제 유입구를 유동 구조 및 열 혼합에 맥동시키는 효과

title: Development of an equivalent homogenization method with anisotropic scattering few-group constants in the RMC code
abstract: The Legendre expansion, widely adopted for representing anisotropic scattering in Monte Carlo multi-group cross section generation, suffers from truncation artifacts that can lead to negative scattering cross sections. This paper develops an angle-discretized macroscopic scattering matrix representation, generated by direct track-length tallying during continuous-energy Monte Carlo transport and used as the working representation throughout a complete Monte Carlo two-step workflow in the Reactor Monte Carlo code RMC. The representation is non-negative by construction across all angular bins, avoiding the negative scattering cross sections that arise from Legendre truncation. Supporting engineering elements required for the complete workflow—including a full-core tallying scheme that mitigates environmental-effect errors associated with reflective single-assembly boundary conditions, and a Monte Carlo–adapted SPH iteration for use within the workflow—are also described. The methodology is validated on a PWR assembly, a MOX fuel assembly with control-rod insertion and withdrawal, a four-assembly mini-core, and the C5G7 benchmark. Reference solutions are obtained from continuous-energy RMC simulations, and the angle-discretized scattering matrices are compared against OpenMC Legendre-expansion results to illustrate the non-negativity property of the proposed representation. Key results include a reduction of the mini-core eigenvalue deviation from approximately 600 pcm under reflective-boundary group constants to 6 pcm under full-core group constants.
title_ko: RMC 코드에서 이방성 산란 소집단 상수를 갖는 동등한 균질화 방법의 개발

title: Development and validation of the premixing-phase model in the three-dimensional fuel–coolant interaction code SEINA-3D
abstract: Premixing during a fuel–coolant interaction determines the three-dimensional melt–water–vapor state available to a subsequent steam explosion. This study develops and validates the premixing-phase model of the three-dimensional fuel–coolant interaction code SEINA-3D. The model advances five coupled Eulerian material fields—liquid coolant, vapor, connected melt jet, melt droplets, and melt fragments—in one pressure-based framework. Mixed finite-volume/finite-difference discretization, explicit/implicit advancement, and improved SIMPLEPC pressure coupling form the numerical core; VOF–PLIC interface geometry and continuum-surface-force capillarity resolve the connected interfaces; and interphase exchange, breakup, and phase-change closures couple the fields. The Ransom faucet problem, SPHERIC Test 2, and a three-dimensional rising-bubble benchmark verify the transport, free-surface, and capillary treatments, while FARO L-24 validates the complete model under prototypical corium–water conditions. On the finest SPHERIC grid, the median NRMSE is 0.159 over the four water-level records and 0.139 over the eight pressure records, and the first P1 impact amplitude is reproduced within 10.2 %. The rising-bubble calculation preserves the gas volume and reproduces the published centroid, velocity, sphericity, and directional-size endpoints to within 5 %. In the 15-point FARO pressure comparison, the steam-only calculation has an RMSE of about 0.18 MPa and reproduces the approximately 2.2 MPa peak near 1.6 s; adding the reported L-24 hydrogen source raises the late-time pressure by about 0.48 MPa and quantifies the coupled sensitivity of the steam, noncondensable-gas, and headspace closures. The calculation also yields the material inventories, energy partition, void, azimuthal asymmetry, and a debris-size distribution consistent with the post-test recovery. These results establish the premixing capability of SEINA-3D and provide three-dimensional mixture states for steam-explosion load analysis.
title_ko: 3차원 연료 냉각수 상호 작용 코드 SEINA-3D에서 프리믹싱 단계 모델의 개발 및 검증

title: A Bayesian regularized MLEM hybrid approach for reactor fast-neutron spectrum adjustment
abstract: Precise characterization of the fast-neutron energy spectrum constitutes a fundamental requirement for evaluating radiation damage in reactor pressure vessels (RPV). Conventional MLEM iterative adjustment algorithms applied to high-precision spectrum adjustment often result in potential spectral artifacts due to the inability to rigorously propagate off-diagonal covariance terms. A novel Bayesian Regularized Maximum Likelihood Expectation Maximization (BR-MLEM) framework is proposed to address these challenges by integrating hierarchical Bayesian priors with adaptive regularization. This methodology systematically incorporates covariance matrices associated with the prior spectrum, response functions, and measurements, employing singular value decomposition (SVD)-based Monte Carlo sampling to mitigate noise amplification. Application to the H. B. Robinson Unit 2 benchmark demonstrates the algorithm’s capability to produce physically consistent spectra while effectively suppressing non-physical distortions observed in standard MLEM iterations. The adjusted calculated specific activity exhibits excellent agreement with experimental dosimetry data, achieving consistency comparable to generalized least-squares methods but with superior stability in high-energy regions. Posterior uncertainty analysis reveals a significant reduction in relative standard deviations across primary fast-neutron energy groups. These findings confirm that the BR-MLEM framework enhances the fidelity of fluence estimation and provides a robust tool for RPV lifetime management.
title_ko: 원자로 고속 중성자 스펙트럼 조정을 위한 베이지안 정규 MLEM 하이브리드 접근법
